facts.statement: The genus Janiosteus was described by Ivanov in 1988.
The type species of the genus is Janiosteus timanicus.
Fossils of Janiosteus have been found in Timan, Russia.
Janiosteus lived during the Middle Devonian, specifically the Late Givetian stage.
Janiosteus belongs to the class Placodermi.
The parent group of Janiosteus is the family Panxiosteidae.
Janiosteus lived from the Givetian to the Frasnian, between 387.95 and 372.15 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Givetian to Frasnian (387.95 to 372.15 million years ago)

facts.statement: A 2010 study suggested that the family Panxiosteidae was the sister taxon to Dunkleosteidae.
facts.quote: In the 2010 Carr & Hlavin phylogenetic study, Panxiosteidae was recognized as the sister taxon to the family Dunkleosteidae

facts.statement: A 2016 study using a larger dataset placed Panxiosteidae outside Dunkleosteoidea, instead within Coccosteomorphi.
facts.quote: the subsequent 2016 Zhu et al. study using a larger morphological dataset recovered Panxiosteidae well outside of Dunkleosteoidea, instead within Coccosteomorphi

rejected.statement: Janiosteus is an extinct monospecific genus of placoderm arthrodire.
rejected.quote: extinct monospecific genus of placoderm arthrodire
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'Janiosteus is an extinct monospecific genus of placoderm'
